bug_semantics: CWE-306 missing authentication on FastAPI POST /query: any network caller can submit a natural-language QueryRequest that the backend feeds to Interaction.think(), which routes to CoderAgent and other agents. CoderAgent auto-executes LLM-emitted ```bash``` blocks via BashInterpreter.execute([block]) with the safety confirmation flag defaulting to False, then subprocess.Popen(command, shell=True). The unix/windows command blocklist (safety.is_unsafe / is_any_unsafe) is substring-based and omits common RCE primitives (curl, wget, nc, python -c, bash -c, reverse shells), so it does not stop host-level code execution. At the advisory snapshot fc242c7 the API bound uvicorn to 0.0.0.0 with default port 7777, docker-compose published ${BACKEND_PORT:-7777}:${BACKEND_PORT:-7777} on all interfaces, and CORS allow_origins was ['*'], so a network-adjacent (or browser-origin) attacker needed no credential.
flaw_origin: The first public write of the unauthenticated network query API is d1954ff32621e57654bfe08cdcfe5bc51eb8b2fa (2025-04-14, 'First front & backend integration'). That commit added app.py with @app.post('/query') process_query, no auth dependency, uvicorn.run(..., host='0.0.0.0', port=8000), and a direct call to interaction.think() on request.query. The CoderAgent/BashInterpreter/Popen(shell=True) sink already existed for the local CLI; this commit is what exposed that sink as a remote unauthenticated function. Immediate parent 592c7e691550470578a8d8af7a029e4abc59370c ('pre-backend implementation') has schemas.py but no FastAPI app, no /query route, and no uvicorn bind. Later 81b772df9a6757e01cbed13994d24d431684b106 rewrote the same unauthenticated endpoint into a new api.py (parent still had the flaw in app.py) and is a refactor, not a BIC. Wildcard CORS was first applied on app.py in a32cf609588b09f033d5ee18706f5779b266735e, briefly narrowed in 713c01193fb513e1e68dd1d66c7190b330ec164c, then restored to ['*'] in 54cc2a03ec755f8a9c787bdbb26f3bfb7dcfc731. Default port 7777 is a6cf09673b6fbb737b3f36751f7c58fd8cdcfba4. PR #508 (ada287e / merge 8cafc51, 2026-07-02) only changed default bind/CORS and left /query unauthenticated.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-72776/GHSA-wrjr-rgfw-cm84 is a live published CWE-306, not withdrawn or rejected. The critical function is POST /query, which at fc242c7 was reachable on 0.0.0.0:7777 with wildcard CORS and no credential, and which drives agents that execute shell via BashInterpreter Popen(shell=True) without an interactive safety prompt. That is a real unauthenticated RCE chain, not a false positive. The BIC is the smallest public commit that first wrote those unauthenticated query lines and the 0.0.0.0 bind that makes them remotely callable: d1954ff adding app.py. Parent 592c7e69 was checked directly and lacks any FastAPI /query server; the CLI interpreters already existed and are the sink, not the missing-auth introduction. 81b772df's new api.py is a same-mechanism rewrite while app.py on its parent still served unauthenticated /query, so it is not the BIC under the move/refactor rule. CORS * and port 7777 are later exposure amplifiers, not first-writes of the missing-auth mechanism. PR #508 is an incomplete network-exposure mitigation after the advisory snapshot. The cited fix is f1eb2cf (landed by merge ae57a23), which first attaches an auth dependency to /query; CVE marks everything before that SHA affected. AI is judged only on the BIC object: human maintainer author/committer, empty trailers, not a bot, so NOT_AI.
